title: Investigation recipes for slow token paths
content:
Purpose
This note collects pragmatic, investigator-friendly recipes for triaging end-to-end latency problems that show up as “slow token emission” or high per-token latency in the inference path. Aim: give oncall / SRE / engs a short checklist + queries + trace-span patterns they can run through in order, minimizing context switching.

Scope and context
- Applies to streaming/generation requests where per-token latency matters (chat, code-completion, streaming APIs).
- Focus is on production-facing observability artifacts: metric definitions we rely on in dashboards, trace attributes we lean on, and compact runbook steps that point to exact widgets or SQL.
- Not a replacement for the full span/schema docs — this is a rapid-investigation playbook.

Quick triage checklist (3–7 minute run)
1) Check global latency panel: p50/p90/p99 token-emit-time across regions for the last 15 minutes. Is it localized to one region?
2) If localized, filter by model variant and tenant. Is it a single tenant spike? If so, flag tenant isolation, run tenant-specific query (see SQL snippet).
3) Inspect batch-size distribution panel. Did average batch size jump? High variance can cause stalls.
4) Open a representative trace (use trace sampling panel). Look for long spans with names: queue.wait, schedule.wait, model.forward, token.emit. Identify the dominant span.
5) If model.forward dominates, check GPU utilization + memory pressure widget and recent kernel-selection rollouts.
6) If queue.wait / schedule.wait dominates, check autoscaler events and scheduler logs.
7) If token.emit dominates (but model.forward is normal), suspect serialization/streaming/backpressure or network egress. Check network egress metrics and front-end buffer queues.

Metric definitions (for panels and alerts)
- token_emit_time_ms: time from model token ready -> token sent to client (ms). Aggregations: p50/p90/p99 per minute, broken down by region, model_variant, tenant_id.
- model_forward_time_ms: time spent in model compute (single-step forward) excluding KV lookup and queue delays.
- kv_lookup_ms: time spent reading KV cache for prefix/state (avg + p95). Also track kv_cache_miss_rate (ratio of requests with miss).
- input_queue_time_ms: time spent waiting in request queue before being scheduled onto a batch. This is where autoscaler/scheduling regressions appear.
- batch_size_distribution: histogram of batch sizes (0–1, 2–4, 5–8, 9+). Useful for sudden changes when batching logic regresses.
- tail_latency_tickets: count of requests where token_emit_time_ms > threshold (configurable by model class).
- link metrics: gpu_util_pct, host_network_tx_ms, scheduler_pending_count.

Recommended trace span design and attributes (what an investigator needs)
- Span names (short): recv.request, queue.wait, batch.assemble, schedule.wait, model.forward, kv.read, kv.miss, token.emit, response.serialize.
- Required attributes on root span: request_id, tenant_id, model_name, model_variant, seq_len, prompt_token_count, requested_max_tokens, streaming_enabled (bool), route (api_route).
- Span-level attributes we care about: batch_size, gpu_id, kv_cache_hit (bool), cpu_steal_pct, kernel_name, host_region, node_type (gpu/cpu), autoscaler_event_id.
- Breadcrumbs: include short sample of prompt-length bucket and a hash/personalization label to correlate similar requests. Avoid including PII.

Sampling strategy notes (practical)
- Default adaptive approach: always sample all traces where token_emit_time_ms > p95 for the tenant (severity-weighted sampling).
- Low-traffic tenants: sample 1/100 by default but increase to 1/10 on any p90 spike.
- Canary/rollout: force 100% sampling for model_variant under canary for first 24h.

Dashboard widgets and investigative panels (suggested layout)
Top row (fast overview):
- Live tail: rolling p50/p90/p99 token_emit_time_ms (15m window) — global or per-region toggle.
- Error + backpressure counters: token_dropped, egress_retries, stream_timeouts.
- Batch size heatmap: bucketed by seq_len (rows) vs batch size (cols) with counts.

Detail row (investigation):
- Span breakdown waterfall: avg time per span (queue, schedule, forward, kv, emit) at p50/p90/p99. Clickable to filter traces.
- KV cache warmth panel: prefix hit rate by tenant cohort + recent churn.
- Model compute vs GPU utilization: scatter plot with forward_time_ms vs gpu_util_pct (helps find noisy hosts).

Token-path debug row (operators):
- Token emission timeline: per-request timeline showing timestamps for recv.request -> token.emit by token index (aggregate sample of 50).
- Network egress latency & retransmits for streaming sockets.
- Autoscaler events and recent scaling decisions overlayed on timeline.

Example SQL / metrics queries (Prometheus/Clickhouse-style pseudo queries)
- Identify tenants with most tail tokens in last 1h:
  SELECT tenant_id, countIf(token_emit_time_ms > 200) AS slow_tokens
  FROM token_emits
  WHERE ts >= now() - interval 1 hour
  GROUP BY tenant_id
  ORDER BY slow_tokens DESC

- Correlate batch size change with token latency (15m buckets):
  SELECT time_bin, avg(batch_size) AS avg_batch, quantile(0.9)(token_emit_time_ms) AS p90_emit
  FROM batch_events JOIN token_emits USING (request_id)
  WHERE ts >= now() - interval 2 hour
  GROUP BY time_bin
  ORDER BY time_bin DESC

Runbook snippets (what to do once you find the dominant span)
- model.forward long: check kernel-selection/quantization flags rolled out in last 24h (linked PRs). Check GPU host logs for OOMs or throttling. Consider routing to a compatible lower-latency variant as temporary fallback.
- queue.wait long: check scheduler backlog, open autoscaler UI, increase scale target temporarily, and add a 5m note on the incident timeline.
- kv.read long or high miss rate: backfill cache for hot prefixes or temporarily enable warm-cache routing. Contact model-onboarding for recent tokenization changes.
- token.emit long: confirm streaming proxy health and front-end buffer sizes. Consider switching to batch-flush on a short interval to reduce emit overhead for small tokens.

Investigation examples (short vignettes)
- Vignette A: p99 jump in token_emit_time for US-WEST only. Found model_forward p99 normal, queue.wait spiked due to a single noisy tenant causing large batch size variance. Action: isolate tenant, throttle, schedule tenant patch to smaller max_batch.
- Vignette B: token_emit_time elevated but model_forward low. Traces showed token.emit span had high time and host_network_tx_ms high. Root cause: kernel upgrade increased serialization overhead in streaming layer. Action: rollback kernel, open gearbox PR.

Open questions / TODOs
- Define a compact token-level SLI with 3-second budget for 95% of tokens for conversational models. Need product agreement.
- Automate an investigator notebook that auto-loads a representative trace + fills in the triage checklist fields.
- Add tenant-level warm-cache alert (kv_cache_miss_rate > 0.3 sustained for 10m).

Notes to self / quick links
- Use the \"trace playground\" to compare before/after traces for canary variants.
- See linked artifacts for current token span spec and PR history.

If you take this doc and iterate: help me add exact PromQL snippets for the dashboards and a sample Grafana panel JSON for the token emission timeline.

-- Riley
